newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Swedish FinMin says does not support devaluations.
newsitem.headline: Swedish FinMin says does not support devaluations.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday he did not support devaluations and denied the possibility of devaluing the crown was a reason for staying outside Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
He said that equally strict economic policies were needed for countries staying outside EMU as for those within the union.
When asked by Reuters if a reason for the ruling Social Democrats decision to keep Sweden outside EMU at the start in 1999 was the possibility to devalue the crown, Asbrink said:
"No, it isn't. I don't have that view. I'm not a supporter of devaluations."

Asbrink repeated that Sweden outside EMU must pursue "at least as strict economic policies" as countries within the union. Such policies would not lead to a softer crown, rather the opposite, he said.
"(I) don't have the slightest inclination to devalue...that is an unfortunate misunderstanding."
The crown softened to 4.5140 against the mark early on Monday from 4.4910 late on Friday after a Swedish news agency reported that Asbrink had raised the spectre of devaluation.
But Asbrink's comments in Luxembourg, where he was reviewing why Sweden decided not to join EMU, were referring to monetary policy mechanisms available to countries outside EMU.
Asked if he was discussing devaluation, Asbrink told a news conference there: "Yes, you could say that. But you can equally discuss revaluation."
